# ezghcloud_hosted_queue_rabbitmq_vhost (Resource)

A vhost on a RabbitMQ cluster. New queues are quorum queues unless the app declares another type. Destroying it deletes this vhost alone, and is refused while it holds queues.



<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `cluster_id` (String) Cluster (hqc_) it is in. Changing it replaces the object.
- `name` (String) The vhost's name; default is reserved. Changing it replaces the object.
- `project_id` (String) Project of the cluster. Changing it replaces the object.

### Optional

- `default_queue_type` (String) quorum, classic or stream: the type of a queue declared without one. Changes in place.
- `max_connections` (Number) Most connections to the vhost; null for no limit. Changes in place.
- `max_queues` (Number) Most queues the vhost may hold; null for no limit. Changes in place.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) cluster_id/name, with the vhost before the name for a RabbitMQ object.
- `organization_id` (String) Organization managed by the configured provider.
- `origin` (String) api if it was made through EZGH, broker if an app made it first (an imported object).

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Replace identifiers with values from your organization.
terraform import ezghcloud_hosted_queue_rabbitmq_vhost.example 'ORGANIZATION_ID/PROJECT_ID/CLUSTER_ID/NAME'
```
